title: Release Stewardship: Runway Checklist, Staggered Calendar, and Draft Notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact stewardship playbook for the upcoming release window (week-of 2027-06-14). It focuses on cross-team handoffs, a staggered (takt) calendar for traffic shifts, telemetry gating rules, an abbreviated launch checklist for operators, and a draft of release notes to accompany the roll. Intent: make a single-page operational reference that folks can pin to a tab while they run the release.

Quick summary of what’s changing:
- Model routing: introduce model variant v2-quantized for chat endpoints; fallback remains v2-fp16.
- Serving runtime: enable continuous-batching across 2 dedicated pools (region-us-west-1).
- Observability: new sampling for token-level latency on route /chat/stream; extra traces for prefix cache hits.
- Config: rollout uses 3-stage traffic split (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated rollback on SLO breach.

Owners and on-call contacts:
- Release steward (overall): Avery Chen (runway lead)
- Runtime & infra: Samir Patel (infra lead)
- Model & inference: Riley Gomez (applied-ml lead)
- Observability & SLOs: Morgan Lee (sre/obs lead)
- Customer comms: Priya Srinivasan (customer-success) — listed for release notes and key customer heads-up
Links: Confluence runbook (linked_artifacts[0]), Jira ticket RD-7894, PR #8910. Slack channel: #release-stewards (linked).

Stewardship runway checklist (pre-flight, day -7 -> day 0):
- day -7: finalize PRs; ensure green on e2e smoke (integration with KV cache). Owner: infra
- day -6: QA: run 24h production-like load test at 60% expected QPS for new quantized variant; collect latency distributions. Owner: applied-ml + infra
- day -4: Telemetry audit: verify token-latency histogram buckets, sampling rates, and trace context propagation. Confirm alert thresholds loaded. Owner: obs
- day -3: Canary config prepared in infra: traffic-split manifests, throttle curves, and surge safety lane. Owner: infra
- day -2: Stakeholder sync (30m): product, obs, infra, applied-ml, cs. Walk through canary stop/rollback triggers. Owner: steward
- day -1: Launch rehearsal (dry run): team roles, incident channel, pager rotation check. Owner: steward + sre
- day 0 (launch): follow staggered calendar below and monitor gating rules. Owner: steward

Takt (staggered) calendar — condensed view (all times UTC):
- T+0h (09:00): Deploy model variant v2-quantized to pool-usw1 canary nodes (no traffic). Smoke test (3m).
- T+0h30: Start 5% traffic shift to v2-quantized across region-usw1; monitor 0–30m metrics: p50/p95 latency, error-rate, token-serve-rate, KV cache hit-rate.
- T+1h30: If telemetry green (see gating rules), expand to 25% for next 90m.
- T+3h: If still green, expand to 100% over 30m (incremental steps at 25/50/75/100).
- T+6h: Final verification window; if stable, mark release as rolled.
Notes: keep a 15m quiet-window after each expansion to let traces aggregate.

Gating rules (automated + manual triggers):
Automated rollback triggers (immediate rollback):
- p95 generation latency increases by >30% relative to baseline over a 10m sliding window AND absolute p95 > 1200ms
- aggregate user-facing error rate >0.5% sustained for 5m
- token throughput drop >20% sustained for 5m
Manual stop conditions (operator judgment):
- unexplained rise in tail latency correlated with KV cache misses
- novel errors with more than 5 unique stack traces within 10m
- regression in quality signals from canary promptset eval (human-reviewed)
Operator checklist (during rollout):
- Confirm alerting channels are active and alert thresholds visible.
- Watch metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, token-serve-rate, CPU/GPU utilization on canary nodes, KV cache hit-rate.
- Validate logs for increased RPC retries or timeouts.
- Keep a running notes file (copy entries into PR commentary).
- If rollback occurs: capture pre-rollback snapshot IDs (GC-safe), mark Jira RD-7894 with timeline and revert PR link.

Rollback matrix (quick):
- Soft rollback: shift traffic back to previous variant in 2 steps (100% -> 25% -> 0%) over 30m if early-stage minor issue.
- Hard rollback: full immediately revert to v2-fp16 and hold for postmortem if SLO breach automatic trigger met.

Observability additions for this roll:
- New percentile tracer: token-latency.p99-{route,model_variant} with 1m resolution.
- Extra sampling: 5% full-trace sampling for canary traffic for first 6h.
- Tag traces with commit SHA and model-variant-id.
- Quick dashboards: canary-lite (latency, errors, cache_hit, gpu_util) and canary-debug (sampled traces).

Release notes draft (externally-facing, first-pass):
Title: Live rollout of v2-quantized chat model (June 2027)
Summary: We are deploying an optimized, quantized variant of our v2 chat model that reduces per-token cost while preserving output quality for most workloads. The rollout will be staged over the next several hours with automated safety gates.
What’s new:
- v2-quantized available as a model variant; expected 20–35% lower GPU token cost.
- Improved continuous batching in us-west-1 for chat streaming.
- Enhanced telemetry for token-level latency and prefix cache metrics.
Notes and known limitations:
- Very rare edge-case prompts that stress long KV cache lifetimes may see slight quality differences; we will monitor promptset-based quality regressions.
- Enterprise customers with strict quantization policies may continue to pin to v2-fp16. Contact CS for assistance.
Rollout plan and timeline:
- Staged 5% -> 25% -> 100% over a 6 hour window with safety gates.
Feedback and rollback:
- If you observe regressions, file a ticket referencing RD-7894 and include example inputs/outputs. We will honor rollbacks for critical regressions.

Post-launch actions (first 48h):
- 0–6h: keep enhanced sampling; collect human-eval on curated promptsets every 30m.
- 6–24h: run batch offline eval across production logs (sample), inspect drift.
- 24–48h: stabilize sampling rates back to baseline and finalize release note for public docs.

Open questions and follow-ups (action items):
- (A) Decide final sampling rate after 6h: obs to propose reduced sampling targets. Owner: Morgan. Due: T+5h.
- (B) Confirm billing tag attribution for quantized runs so cost reports reflect savings. Owner: finance-infra liaison (TBD). Due: day +1.
- (C) Validate that model pinning semantics for private deployments propagate the correct variant id. Owner: private-deployments eng. Due: preflight.

Quick-reference snippets for operators (copy/paste):
- K8s canary command: kubectl apply -f canary-manifest-usw1.yaml --record
- Rollback command: kubectl patch svc/chat-routing -p '{"spec":{"trafficSplit":[{"variant":"v2-fp16","percent":100}]}}'
- Trace lookup (sample): traces.search?tag=model_variant:v2-quantized&range=now-6h

Notes to self and unfinished thoughts:
- If we see KV cache-induced tail latency, consider a transient increase to prefix-cache-ttl to avoid cascading recomputes.
- Might be worth adding an automatic short-circuit to route small-context requests to fp16 path to protect p99.
- Keep an eye on autoscaler behavior during batching spikes; add guardrails if necessary.

Appendix: linked artifacts and checkpoints
- Runbook (detailed): https://confluence.redwood.example/display/RUNWAY/Release-Stewardship-2027-06
- Jira ticket: JIRA/RD-7894
- Engineering PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8910
- Slack: #release-stewards

End of draft. Add edits below as we walk through rehearsal.
